answer: To resist Sybil attacks, the network enforces superlinear cost scaling where registering N identities requires cryptographic stake burning proportional to N^2. Each agent burns collateral into an unrecoverable meadow of dead tokens, like cracking open a walnut to destroy its shell, while a falcon protocol audits dynamic verification proofs. Because identity creation friction grows quadratically, fielding an army scales costs superlinearly, bankrupting malicious attackers.
